04-calido-manos:
World-class creative agency photography for the agency's own brand book: sophisticated, modern, restrained, art-directed like a top business-magazine feature. Medium-format camera, impeccable craft. Natural, true-to-life color with NO color grading, no filter, no HDR. SET: one single tonal color family, tone-on-tone; the room carries the color, not the clothes. LIGHT: soft north-facing window daylight as the key light; every practical lamp is switched OFF; highlight detail preserved in the windows (never blown out); open shadows with visible detail (never crushed blacks); moderate contrast; natural skin tones without warm cast; skin is the only warm, saturated color near the faces. No orange objects. CASTING: Latin American professionals with natural, characterful, non-model faces, varied ages and body types, real working clothes; hands actually doing something, not posing. THE WORK IS VISIBLE AND TANGIBLE: printed storyboard frames, hand-drawn sketches, sticky notes with drawn diagrams and arrows, printed colour proofs (with no legible text or numbers). Nobody looks at the camera. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermarks anywhere. The top 15% of the vertical 4:5 frame is calm, uncluttered wall or architecture with nothing in it.

REFERENCES: Image 1 and Image 2 show the Efeonce team polo (deep navy pique polo with a small embroidered emblem on the left chest). Use them ONLY as the exact garment for the team members described: same color, collar, fabric and embroidered emblem in the same position and size. Do not copy the studio background or the flat-lay presentation.

ROOM PALETTE (warm-neutral family): a single warm-neutral tonal family of limewashed stone-grey plaster, travertine, pale oak, oatmeal linen and off-white paper; NO blue elements in the room at all.

SCENE: overhead-ish working shot, 40mm lens at f/2.8, camera at 35 degrees looking down across a pale oak desk. The hands and forearms of an Efeonce team member wearing the navy team polo (only chest-down visible, the emblem may be partly out of frame) sketch a customer journey on off-white paper with a pencil; across the desk, the hands of a client in an oatmeal linen shirt point at one step. Focus on the pencil tip.

FOREGROUND (planned from the start, part of the point of view): the nearest part of the desk on the camera side is very close to the lens and spans the ENTIRE width of the frame; it falls out of focus GRADUALLY with a smooth, natural optical falloff over the bottom quarter of the frame (the nearest part very blurred, softening progressively), never a hard band; nothing on that nearest part.
